engineDefinition: Qualified reusable systems-level machinery exposed through explicit semantic composition and runtime boundaries so application authors do not repeatedly reconstruct infrastructure.

jtfThesis.reason: Copeland/TSON, Dominatus, Aurelian, Machina.UI, and TinyFarm have coherent ownership, while several application-facing kits remain locally implemented.

currentAurelianRole: World, actuation, runtime, renderer-neutral render contracts, raster/null/native graphics, assets, and shaders; implementation remains render-infrastructure-heavy.
formalAurelianRole: Agentic interactive application and world runtime with native rendering as one backend capability.

laws.scene: validated table contents plus graph composition plus reducer routing plus semantic state truth plus projection-only rendering
laws.realization: active scene uses detailed spatial realization; inactive scene uses coarse semantic progression
laws.controllers: controller produces typed intent; resolver alone mutates authoritative state
laws.time: host, render, locomotion, world, and agent-decision time are distinct
laws.content: TSON loads through validation and canonicalization into typed catalogs; raw rows are never runtime authority
laws.presentation: application state projects to semantic UI and world frames; replaceable backends realize them

canonicalScenario: M21 checkpoint composition: hotbar selection, Chop, Gather, Cook, dungeon routing, Attack, semantic hashes; enclosing proof adds save/load, replay/repeat, projection/DTO, and peaceful host isolation.
